papers.title: Loss of the clock protein PERIOD1 causes sex-specific impacts on the heart in Dahl salt-sensitive rats.
papers.abstract: Salt-sensitive (SS) hypertension is a driver of cardiovascular disease. Circadian biology is implicated in hypertension. One component of the circadian molecular clock, the protein PERIOD1 (PER1), is involved in blood pressure regulation. We previously published that loss of PER1 (PER1 KO) in a rat model of SS hypertension, the Dahl SS rat, is associated with exacerbated renal injury and hypertension, as well as disrupted circadian regulation of heart rate. The cardiac and sex-specific impacts of PER1 KO in SS hypertension are undetermined. We utilized male and female PER1 KO and Dahl SS rats to investigate changes in the cardiac transcriptome, revealing sex-dependent shifts in gene expression. Male PER1 KO rats exhibited upregulation of genes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling. Consistent with this, male, but not female PER1 KO rats showed higher cardiac fibrosis compared to their Dahl SS counterparts. Terminal measurements revealed that male, but not female PER1 KO rats had increased blood pressure compared to Dahl SS controls. Given the lack of an apparent phenotype in females, only male subjects were used for subsequent ultrasound echocardiography studies. We determined longitudinal in vivo cardiac function in male rats during normal salt and 14 days of high salt diet. This revealed reduced stroke volume and decreased cardiac output at baseline, prior to exposure to high salt diet in male PER1 KO rats. These results indicate that impaired cardiac function may predispose PER1 KO rats to salt-sensitive hypertension.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

papers.title: Aβ42 induces selective degeneration in hippocampal cells of aged monkeys.
papers.abstract: The hippocampus is one of the earliest and most severely affected brain regions in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is critical for memory formation. However, the precise mechanisms through which AD disrupts hippocampal neurons remain poorly understood. To investigate the effects of Aβ42 in a model closer to humans, we performed stereotaxic injections of an adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) vector encoding human Aβ42 into the hippocampus of young (7-year-old) and aged (>20-year-old) cynomolgus monkeys. We found that AAV9-mediated Aβ42 expression induced more severe neuropathology, reduced daytime activity, and increased sleep disturbances in aged monkeys compared to young controls. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed an age-dependent reduction in disease-associated microglia subtype II (DAM II) in the aged hippocampus. Furthermore, we identified a specific subtype of hippocampal pyramidal neurons (PCs) ( TRPS1 + RELN +) that is selectively vulnerable to Aβ42 toxicity in aged monkeys. Our findings indicate that Aβ42 toxicity is exacerbated in the aged primate hippocampus due to a combination of microglial decline and the selective vulnerability of a distinct neuronal subtype ( TRPS1 + RELN + PCs). This identified subtype represents a new potential therapeutic target for treating hippocampal dysfunction in AD.

papers.title: Prototype-based geometry of local object patches in the pigeon mesopallium ventrolaterale.
papers.abstract: In natural vision, objects are frequently partially occluded and thus perceived through local fragments, yet how such fragments are organized in neural representational space remains poorly understood. Using pigeons ( Columba livia) as a model, we combined behavior from a whole-part image categorization paradigm with population electrophysiological recordings from the mesopallium ventrolaterale (MVL) during passive viewing. We used Contrastive Embedding for Behavioral and Representational Analysis-time (CEBRA) to embed neural time series into a low-dimensional space, defined category neural prototypes from population responses to whole images, and projected local patches into the same space to quantify their distances to the prototypes. This framework allowed systematic tests of how prototype distance relates to behavioral accuracy and patch semantics. In MVL, animal categories formed compact, prototype-centered clusters. Across patches, greater prototype distance predicted lower behavioral accuracy, and patches closer to the prototype were enriched for diagnostic semantic parts (e.g., heads and faces). By contrast, across multiple deep-network baselines, prototype distance neither reliably predicted behavior nor consistently reflected the semantic distribution of patches. Building on these baselines, we then introduced a local prototype learning mechanism in which category matching is governed by the proximity between local features and learned prototypes. The resulting network reproduced several MVL-consistent geometric signatures, including prototype-centered clustering for animal categories and a negative relationship between prototype distance and behavior. Together, these results support the hypothesis that incomplete-object representations in pigeon MVL are organized by a diagnostic-part-related prototype geometry, and suggest that this geometry provides actionable neural constraints for brain-inspired vision models.

papers.title: Regular physical activity and a 12-week structured exercise program: Associations with circadian organization and sleep in permanent night-shift workers.
papers.abstract: Permanent night-shift work induces circadian misalignment, sleep disruption, and impaired physiological organization. Although exercise is increasingly recognized as a non-photic zeitgeber, its long-term association with circadian adaptation under occupational conditions remains poorly understood. To examine whether habitual physical activity and a 12-week supervised exercise program are associated with circadian organization, sleep, and physiological rhythms in permanent night-shift workers. Study 1 was a cross-sectional comparison of 12 habitually physically active and 12 sedentary permanent night-shift workers matched for major demographic and occupational characteristics. Study 2 was an uncontrolled longitudinal before-after intervention in 16 initially sedentary workers. Using the same ambulatory protocol, activity-rest rhythms, oral temperature, sleep, and neuromuscular, respiratory, cardiovascular, and cognitive variables were repeatedly assessed across an entire work-rest cycle. Habitually physically active workers exhibited greater rhythm amplitude, dominant oscillatory periods closer to 24 h during the workweek, higher sleep efficiency, and more coherent temporal organization across several physiological systems than sedentary workers. Similar pre-to-post changes were observed in Study 2. During weekend recovery, dominant oscillatory periods transiently shortened to approximately 18-22 h, concurrently with rapid repositioning of activity-rest and oral-temperature acrophases toward diurnal timing. These dynamics most likely reflect adaptive circadian reorganization rather than changes in endogenous circadian period. Regular physical activity was associated with greater circadian robustness, temporal coherence, and better sleep. Because Study 2 lacked a control group, the longitudinal changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the exercise program. Controlled studies using direct phase markers are required.

papers.title: Biopsychosocial Network Associations in Paediatric Chronic Pain: A Cross-Lagged Panel Network Study.
papers.abstract: Biopsychosocial models of chronic pain emphasize interactions between biological, psychological and social processes, yet little is known about their organization over time in paediatric chronic pain. This study examined cross-sectional and longitudinal network associations among pain intensity, pain interference, pain extent, depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, pain catastrophizing, sleep disturbance, fatigue and peer relationships in children and adolescents with chronic pain. The baseline network was estimated using a Gaussian graphical model with regularized partial correlations (N = 744). Cross-lagged panel network models were used to examine autoregressive and cross-lagged associations from baseline to 12 months (n = 357) and 24 months (n = 186) among youth with persistent chronic pain. Pain interference had the highest cross-sectional strength centrality, followed by depressive and anxiety symptoms. Strongest baseline associations involved fatigue-pain interference, anxiety-depressive symptoms, pain catastrophizing-anxiety symptoms and sleep disturbance-pain interference. In the longitudinal models, pain interference showed the most consistent prospective pattern, with associations to later pain catastrophizing at 12 months and to later sleep disturbance and pain catastrophizing at 24 months. Depressive symptoms and pain catastrophizing were more often associated with prior levels of other domains. Findings extend prior cross-sectional evidence by showing that pain interference was highly connected at baseline and prospectively involved among youth with persistent chronic pain. Pain interference may represent an informative functional domain for understanding how pain-related, psychological and physical difficulties are organized over time, supporting the clinical relevance of assessing interference with daily functioning. This study extends paediatric chronic pain research by examining cross-sectional and longitudinal associations among pain-related, psychological, physical and social domains. Pain interference showed the highest connectivity at baseline and was consistently involved in prospective associations, particularly with pain catastrophizing and sleep disturbance. These findings highlight multidomain assessment and suggest that interference with daily functioning may help identify broader pain-related difficulties that could otherwise be missed.

papers.title: Association of questionnaire-defined probable obstructive sleep apnea with advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in US adults: a NHANES study with machine learning analysis.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome integrates cardiovascular disease, kidney disease, and metabolic dysfunction within a prevention-oriented framework, but the population-level association between obstructive sleep apnea and advanced CKM remains unclear. This cross-sectional study included 8,523 adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Survey-weighted logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between questionnaire-defined probable OSA (pOSA) and advanced CKM, with subgroup analyses and interaction tests performed across predefined population groups. Six machine learning models were also developed for exploratory classification of advanced CKM, and Shapley Additive Explanations were used to interpret the selected model. pOSA was more common among participants with advanced CKM than among those with non-advanced stages. In the core multivariable-adjusted survey-weighted model, pOSA was associated with higher odds of advanced CKM; however, after additional adjustment for body mass index categories, the association was attenuated and was no longer statistically significant (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 0.92-1.49, p = 0.197). In the machine learning analysis, XGBoost had the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.876), whereas the random forest model showed favorable calibration with an area under the curve of 0.868 and was selected for interpretation. Age contributed most to the model output, followed by estimated glomerular filtration rate, smoking, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, glycated hemoglobin, and mean systolic blood pressure. These findings suggest a potential association between pOSA and advanced CKM syndrome among United States adults, while highlighting the importance of considering adiposity when interpreting this association.

papers.title: Association between obstructive sleep apnea and severe exertional dyspnea in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Exertional dyspnea is a common and disabling symptom of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The severity of dyspnea may not correspond closely to spirometric impairment. In patients with COPD and coexisting obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), recurrent nocturnal desaturation may represent an additional sleep-related feature relevant to severe exertional dyspnea. We included 758 clinically stable patients with COPD. Severe exertional dyspnea was defined as a modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scale (mMRC) score ≥3. Multivariable logistic regression models evaluated the associations of the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), oxygen desaturation index (ODI), and percentage of sleep time with oxygen saturation below 90% (T90) with severe exertional dyspnea. Participants were predominantly male (92.2%), with a median age of 67.0 years. Severe exertional dyspnea was present in 199 patients (26.3%). After adjusting for confounders, ODI ≥15 was significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.14-2.51, p = 0.009). In contrast, neither AHI ≥15 nor T90 ≥ 10% showed a statistically significant association. In continuous analyses, log(ODI + 1) remained significantly associated with severe exertional dyspnea (OR = 1.27, 95% CI: 1.03-1.57, p = 0.025), whereas log(AHI + 1) and log(T90 + 1) were not statistically significant. Nocturnal ODI was independently associated with severe exertional dyspnea, whereas AHI and T90 were not. The more consistent association for ODI suggests that recurrent nocturnal oxygen desaturations may provide clinically relevant information about the OSA-related component of symptom burden beyond respiratory-event frequency or cumulative nocturnal hypoxemia.

papers.title: Network architecture of sleep, biomarkers, and cognition: Rapid eye movement sleep latency as a cross-domain connector.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD) and related dementias (ADRD) pathology and cognitive decline, but how sleep architecture, biomarkers, and cognition are organized within a conditional dependence framework remains unclear. We studied 98 adults spanning normal cognition (NC; n = 21), mild cognitive impairment (MCI; n = 34), and clinically diagnosed AD dementia (n = 43) using overnight polysomnography, plasma phosphorylated tau181 (p-tau181), neurofilament light chain (NfL), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), amyloid-β positron emission tomography (PET), and multidomain cognitive testing. A regularized Gaussian graphical model was used to characterize conditional associations and identify cross-domain connectivity among sleep, biomarkers, and cognition. The 17-variable network contained 26 edges, with significantly denser within-domain than cross-domain connectivity (40.5% vs 9.6%; p < 0.001). Direct sleep-cognition connections were sparse. Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep latency had the highest bridge strength (0.387), directly connecting the sleep domain with NfL, amyloid-β PET, and BDNF. Plasma p-tau181 was the only biomarker directly connected to global cognition. Exploratory mediation analyses were consistent with indirect associations involving p-tau181 in three of five cognitive domains. Sleep architecture and cognition were conditionally linked primarily through biomarker nodes. REM sleep latency and plasma p-tau181 may represent key cross-domain connectors linking sleep architecture, neurodegeneration, and cognition across the AD continuum.

papers.title: Sleep-cognition associations change direction with proximity to dementia diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Differentiating aspects of sleep health that are modifiable risk factors from prodromal symptoms or consequences of dementia can inform dementia prevention and/or clinical screening efforts, and temporal mapping of sleep-cognition associations can further inform mechanistic hypotheses regarding the role of sleep leading up to dementia diagnosis. We examined bidirectional associations between cognitive function and three modifiable sleep health features, and whether these associations vary by proximity to dementia diagnosis. 291 preclinical dementia participants (median initial age = 83 years, 73% female) and 281 matched cognitively unimpaired 'controls' from the Rush Memory and Aging Project completed up to 11 annual assessments of global cognition (composite of 19 neuropsychological measures) and actigraphy-derived measures of sleep amount, regularity, and timing. Linear mixed-effects models tested whether bidirectional sleep-cognition relationships differed by years-to-dementia diagnosis (preclinical dementia sample) or years-to-last follow-up (matched controls) after adjusting for sociodemographic and health covariates. In the preclinical dementia sample, time-to-dementia modified the effects of sleep amount (both β = 0.02) and regularity (-0.04 < β < 0.02), but not timing, on next-year global cognition. Ten years before dementia diagnosis, longer and more irregular sleep predicted better next-year cognition; 1 year before diagnosis, these sleep patterns predicted worse next-year cognition. While sleep amount unidirectionally predicted subsequent cognition, sleep regularity-cognition associations were consistently bidirectional. These patterns were not observed in matched controls. Changes in sleep-cognition associations over time may differentiate preclinical dementia from normal aging. Future research should investigate the driving mechanisms and modifiability of these sleep-cognition associations.

papers.title: Thermal regulation of ant colonies is driven by biological rhythms and acclimation.
papers.abstract: Activity in hot environments is physiologically costly for ectotherms. In social insect colonies, the division of labor may reduce the costs of physiological performance. Additional mechanisms may include plastic responses to thermal conditions and rhythmic investment into thermal tolerance. Here, we evaluate the extent to which static specialization, biological rhythms, and acclimation account for short-term shifts in thermal performance using a pair of complementary experiments in the tropical ant Ectatomma ruidum. In the first experiment, we marked foraging workers at distinct time periods with differing temperatures, and then compared the thermal tolerance of these workers and non-foragers with a time-to-failure knockdown assay. In the second experiment, we subdivided colonies into three laboratory nests under contrasting thermal regimes and performed the assay at daily thermal minima and maxima. We found thermal tolerance was governed both by acclimation and a daily rhythm. These plastic shifts in thermal tolerance were more substantial than differences among specialized workers. These colonies primarily responded to thermal challenges by flexible changes in thermal tolerance rather than the static differences associated with the division of labor. Our findings demonstrate how modular biological systems may demonstrate greater capacity for resilience to increasing variability in thermal challenges.

papers.title: Rapid and Controlled Single-Nanopore Insertion via Hydrogel-Confined Localized Delivery.
papers.abstract: Controlled insertion of a single protein pore, also referred to as a nanopore, into a free-standing lipid bilayer underpins high-resolution single-channel electrophysiology. Hitherto, conventional bulk reconstitution is stochastic, slow, and prone to multiple insertions. To overcome this, we adapted a hydrogel-confined delivery strategy in which an agarose-filled glass capillary delivers nanopores directly to the bilayer. An optimal window of agarose concentration, aerolysin concentration, and membrane potential raised the single-pore yield to >70% and shortened the waiting time to the first insertion from tens of minutes to a few minutes, without altering native pore conductance. The approach generalizes across the β-barrel toxin aerolysin, the mitochondrial TOM core complex, and a DNA nanopore, making nanopore insertion rapid, controlled, and reproducible.

papers.title: Spreading voltage buildup in high density EEG during migraine aura: A longitudinal single-patient study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate spreading features in surface high-density electroencephalogram (HD-EEG) during migraine aura. Approximately 20%-30% of people with migraine experience migraine with aura (MwA). Migraine aura consists of transient neurological deficits such as visual, sensory, speech, motor, brainstem, or retinal symptoms. Clear features of cortical spreading depolarization (CSD) during migraine aura have recently been demonstrated using intracranial depth electrodes in a patient with MwA and comorbid epilepsy; however, in patients with MwA without comorbid epilepsy, direct detection of CSD in a non-invasive setting is still lacking. We report a longitudinal 256-channel HD-EEG study with a direct coupled amplifier set-up in a 45-year-old patient with MwA, in whom repeated recordings could be acquired during aura including early phases and interictally. Electrodes over the forehead, cheeks, periauricular, and nuchal regions were removed to reduce muscle artifacts, resulting in 172 electrodes. In total, 14 electroencephalograms (EEGs) were acquired, thereof eight during the ictal phase. In two out of four aura recordings with predominantly right homonymous scintillating scotoma, recorded soon after onset, we observed a spreading voltage buildup with contralateral maximum. This was associated with a spreading power increase in the delta frequency band. Voltage increases between neighboring electrodes showed a spread with velocity of estimated at 3.8 mm/min. During auras, increased voltage was observed, predominantly in occipital and temporal electrodes. We suggest that topographically related amplitude buildup and delta spread in temporal relation with aura progression reflects CSD. Since invasive CSD detection has been suggested as a useful neuromonitoring tool, with prognostic and therapeutic relevance, further confirmatory studies for non-invasive CSD detections are warranted.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Disease Prevention in Emerging Adults: A Narrative Review of Hypertension Knowledge, Cardiovascular Risk Perception, Self-Efficacy, and Life's Essential 8 Behaviors.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, making early prevention a public health priority. Emerging adulthood (18-29 years) is a critical period for establishing lifelong cardiovascular health behaviors, yet adherence to the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) health behaviors remains suboptimal among this population. To synthesize evidence on hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, and LE8 health behaviors among emerging adults within the Health Belief Model. A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, APA PsycINFO, and Google Scholar. English-language publications (2000-November 2025) examining hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge, cardiovascular risk perception, self-efficacy, or LE8 health behaviors were reviewed. Findings were synthesized using a Health Belief Model-guided narrative approach. Thirty-nine studies were included. Hypertension-related cardiovascular knowledge alone appeared insufficient to promote sustained engagement in LE8 health behaviors. Emerging adults frequently underestimated their cardiovascular risk despite modifiable risk factors. Self-efficacy may facilitate the translation of cardiovascular risk awareness and motivation into healthy behaviors. The synthesis informed a proposed HBM-guided framework in which knowledge may inform cardiovascular risk perception, risk perception may strengthen motivation for preventive action, and self-efficacy may facilitate healthy eating, physical activity, nicotine avoidance, and adequate sleep. These proposed relationships require empirical testing. Cardiovascular disease prevention among emerging adults requires more than education. Interventions should strengthen cardiovascular risk perception and self-efficacy while addressing social and structural barriers. The proposed framework provides a theory-informed foundation for cardiovascular nursing practice, future research, and intervention development.
